dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. Good afternoon.
Hi hon, good afternoon. Manuel Cabral here. I'm calling about the water coming in the back of my building again. Third time I'm dealing with this, I swear.
Oh no. Okay, let me get some details. Where's the building?

347 Kingston Avenue, up on the Hill. Historic Hill. The building's got a parking lot out back, and the whole lot pitches down toward the back door. So every time it really rains, the water just runs right to the entrance and sits there.
And this was after the storm over the weekend?

Yeah, that nor'easter, Saturday into Sunday. Saturday night it started coming up on the step, and by Sunday morning it was over the threshold. I was out there at six with a push broom, hon, in my slippers.
That's no way to spend a Sunday. Is there a storm drain in the lot, or near it?

There's a catch basin at the low corner, but it's packed with leaves and who knows what. Nothing goes down it. And I know that one's not mine to fix, or maybe it is, I don't know, that's why I'm calling you. Somebody's gotta tell me who owns the problem.

Fair enough. If it's on the city side or tied into the street system, we'd look at it. If it's a private lot drain, that can be different. We'd need to have someone go see it. Is the water getting inside the building?
A little, yeah. Came under the door, soaked the mat and the first few feet of the hallway. Not a disaster but it keeps happening and nobody ever fixes it. I called last time and, you know, nothing.
I'm sorry about that. I don't see a lot of detail in front of me right now, so let me write this up fresh so it gets to the right crew.
Please. And I took pictures. I got the water at the door, the drain with the leaves, the whole lot from the second floor window. I can send them, whatever you need.
That would help a lot. I can give you where to send them in a second. First, is the lot open to the public, or is it just for the building?
Just the building. Tenants and me. It's off the alley, back side. But the water, some of it I think comes down from the street side, runs down the driveway, so who knows.
Okay, that's useful. So the water's coming from both the lot slope and possibly runoff from the street.

Right, right. Sorry, I talk fast. My mother always says I talk like the building's on fire. She's at the kitchen table every morning with the newspaper, reads it out loud to me, every article, whether I want it or not. So I'm half listening to the zoning meeting and half trying to tell you this.
[pause] Ha, well, you're doing fine. Is it still wet back there today?
Still puddled by the drain, yeah. Door's dry now, I mopped. But if we get any more rain this week, same thing.
Understood. I'll note that the drain looks clogged, the lot slopes toward the entrance, and it flooded after the weekend storm. I'll send it to the crew that handles drainage so they can inspect.
And can somebody call me back when it's done? Or even before, if they gotta come look. I'm around, I'm in and out but my cell, well, the number you've got should be on the screen, but I'll give it.
Go ahead and give it to me anyway.
Four oh one, five five five, oh one eight eight. Got it. And it's Manuel Cabral, C-A-B-R-A-L?
That's it. Manuel with an E-L, hon, not the fancy way.
Got it. I'll put a note asking for a call back once the work is done, and for them to reach you if they need access.
Perfect. Now how do I get you these pictures?
You can send them to the Public Works general inbox. I'd rather read it to you slowly so you've got it right. Do you have something to write with?
Hold on, hold on. [pause] Okay, pen's in my hand, go.

Actually, you know what, let me do this better. I'll have someone from the office reach out to you and they can tell you the best way to send them with your report number. That way they're attached to the right file.
Okay, that works. As long as somebody actually calls this time.
I hear you. It'll be on the ticket that you want a call, and I'll mark it as a repeat problem at that address.
Good, because it is. Every storm. I'm not asking for a miracle, just clear the drain and look at how that lot's pitched.
Understood. They'll check the basin first, and then look at whether the grading is something that needs more than a cleaning.
And if it's the landlord's, I mean, I am the landlord, but if it's on the lot owner or whatever, they'll tell me?
Yes, they should tell you which part is the city's and which part is yours to handle.
Fair enough. Alright. How long, you think, before somebody comes out?
After a storm like that, the crews have a backlog, so it may be a few days. Sooner if it's a clear city drain.
A few days. Okay. I'll keep the broom handy.

Let me read it back. 347 Kingston Avenue, Historic Hill, back parking lot, clogged catch basin, water running to the rear entrance after the weekend nor'easter, photos available, callback requested at 401-555-0188.
That's the whole thing. Thanks, hon, I appreciate it. You have a good afternoon.
You too, Mr. Cabral. Take care.
